gaps.sentence: There's still a lot of paperwork ___ (complete) before we can close the account.
gaps.explanation: Noun + passive to-infinitive (paperwork to be completed) — the paperwork receives the action.

gaps.sentence: By this time tomorrow, the results ___ to every candidate.
gaps.explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires future perfect passive: will have been + emailed.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of homes ___ (flood) when the river burst its banks.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive: were + flooded. The cause (the river) is in the when-clause.

gaps.sentence: Too much time ___ (waste) on pointless meetings these days.
gaps.explanation: 'These days' signals a present general situation: is + wasted (singular 'time').

gaps.sentence: These wires must ___ by a qualified electrician.
gaps.explanation: After a modal, passive = be + past participle: must be checked. 'Been' needs 'have'.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript is too fragile ___ (handle) without gloves.
gaps.explanation: Passive to-infinitive: to be + past participle. The manuscript receives the handling.

gaps.sentence: Your luggage ___ (weigh) at check-in, so allow extra time.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + weighed. The agent (staff) is obvious.

gaps.sentence: The winners ___ a trophy at the closing ceremony.
gaps.hint: passive of a verb with two objects
gaps.explanation: Give somebody something → somebody is given something: future passive will be + given.
